# Proof

We compute $\pi_1(G/G_x)$ using the long exact homotopy sequence of the fibration $G_x \hookrightarrow G \to G/G_x$.

**Key facts:**

1. **$G$ is simply connected and connected**, so $\pi_1(G) = 0$ and $\pi_0(G) = 0$ (the one-point set).

2. **$G_x$ is connected**, so $\pi_0(G_x) = 0$. Here is the argument. Since $G$ is compact, $\mathfrak{g}^* \cong \mathfrak{g}$ via an $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant inner product, so the coadjoint action identifies with the adjoint action. Conjugating, we may assume (the element of $\mathfrak{g}$ corresponding to) $x$ lies in a fixed Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{t}$. The isotropy group $G_x = \{g \in G : \operatorname{Ad}(g)x = x\}$ is then the centralizer in $G$ of the torus $S = \overline{\{\exp(tx) : t \in \mathbb{R}\}}$ (the closure of the one-parameter subgroup generated by $x$). A classical theorem (Borel; see also Bröcker–tom Dieck) states that **the centralizer of a torus in a compact connected Lie group is connected**. Hence $G_x = C_G(S)$ is connected.

**Long exact sequence.** The projection $G \to G/G_x$ is a principal $G_x$-bundle, hence a (Serre) fibration with fiber $G_x$. Its long exact homotopy sequence contains the segment
$$\pi_1(G_x) \xrightarrow{\;i_*\;} \pi_1(G) \xrightarrow{\;j_*\;} \pi_1(G/G_x) \xrightarrow{\;\partial\;} \pi_0(G_x) \xrightarrow{\;i_*\;} \pi_0(G).$$

Substituting $\pi_1(G) = 0$, $\pi_0(G_x) = 0$, and $\pi_0(G) = 0$:
$$\pi_1(G_x) \longrightarrow 0 \longrightarrow \pi_1(G/G_x) \longrightarrow 0 \longrightarrow 0.$$

By exactness at $\pi_1(G/G_x)$:
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_1(G/G_x) \to \pi_0(G_x)\bigr) = \operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_1(G) \to \pi_1(G/G_x)\bigr).$$
The left-hand side is $\ker(\pi_1(G/G_x) \to 0) = \pi_1(G/G_x)$, and the right-hand side is $\operatorname{im}(0 \to \pi_1(G/G_x)) = 0$. Therefore
$$\pi_1(G/G_x) = 0.$$

**Conclusion.** The fundamental group of the coadjoint orbit $G/G_x$ is trivial:
$$\boxed{\pi_1(G/G_x) = 0.}$$

The three ingredients — simple connectivity of $G$ (giving $\pi_1(G)=0$), connectedness of $G$ (giving $\pi_0(G)=0$), and connectedness of the isotropy group $G_x$ (giving $\pi_0(G_x)=0$, via the theorem that centralizers of tori in compact connected Lie groups are connected) — together force $\pi_1(G/G_x)$ to vanish.

Conjugating, we may assume (the element of $\mathfrak{g}$ corresponding to) $x$ lies in a fixed Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{t}$. The isotropy group $G_x = \{g \in G : \operatorname{Ad}(g)x = x\}$ is then the centralizer in $G$ of the torus $S = \overline{\{\exp(tx) : t \in \mathbb{R}\}}$ (the closure of the one-parameter subgroup generated by $x$). A classical theorem (Borel; see also Bröcker–tom Dieck) states that **the centralizer of a torus in a compact connected Lie group is connected**. Hence $G_x = C_G(S)$ is connected.

**Long exact sequence.** The projection $G \to G/G_x$ is a principal $G_x$-bundle, hence a (Serre) fibration with fiber $G_x$. Its long exact homotopy sequence contains the segment
$$\pi_1(G_x) \xrightarrow{\;i_*\;} \pi_1(G) \xrightarrow{\;j_*\;} \pi_1(G/G_x) \xrightarrow{\;\partial\;} \pi_0(G_x) \xrightarrow{\;i_*\;} \pi_0(G).$$

Substituting $\pi_1(G) = 0$, $\pi_0(G_x) = 0$, and $\pi_0(G) = 0$:
$$\pi_1(G_x) \longrightarrow 0 \longrightarrow \pi_1(G/G_x) \longrightarrow 0 \longrightarrow 0.$$

By exactness at $\pi_1(G/G_x)$:
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_1(G/G_x) \to \pi_0(G_x)\bigr) = \operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_1(G) \to \pi_1(G/G_x)\bigr).$$

$$\boxed{\pi_1(G/G_x) = 0.}$$
